plainLanguageExplanation: Serves as the liquid base that dissolves other ingredients and helps create the product texture.
sensitivityNotes: Well tolerated by almost all skin types. Essential for hydrating formulas.
evidenceOrReference: Cosmetic Ingredient Review (CIR) Safety Assessment

plainLanguageExplanation: Attracts water molecules into the outer layer of skin, helping maintain essential hydration.
sensitivityNotes: Extremely low irritation potential; suitable for sensitive and compromised skin barriers.
evidenceOrReference: CIR Safety Assessment; Journal of Dermatological Science 2008

plainLanguageExplanation: A multi-tasking vitamin that helps improve the skin barrier, even skin tone, and balance oil production.
sensitivityNotes: Usually very gentle, though temporary flushing or mild tingling can occur at higher concentrations (above 5-10%).
evidenceOrReference: Dermatologic Surgery 2005; British Journal of Dermatology

plainLanguageExplanation: A salt form of hyaluronic acid that binds water to keep the skin surface supple and plump.
sensitivityNotes: Rarely causes irritation. Functions best in formulas balanced with occlusives or emollients.
evidenceOrReference: International Journal of Toxicology 2009

plainLanguageExplanation: Naturally occurring lipid that reinforces the skin's lipid matrix, reducing moisture loss.
sensitivityNotes: Biocompatible with natural skin barrier; low risk of irritation or sensitivity.
evidenceOrReference: Skin Pharmacology and Physiology 2008; CIR Assessment

plainLanguageExplanation: A botanical herb traditionally used to calm visible redness, irritation, and stressed skin.
sensitivityNotes: Generally mild and well-tolerated; botanical extracts can rarely cause contact allergy in sensitized individuals.
evidenceOrReference: Phytomedicine Journal 2012; Indian Journal of Dermatology

plainLanguageExplanation: Converts to pantothenic acid in the skin to aid barrier restoration, soothe irritation, and improve elasticity.
sensitivityNotes: Low irritation profile; widely used in after-sun and post-treatment formulas.
evidenceOrReference: Journal of Cosmetic Science 2011; CIR Safety Assessment

plainLanguageExplanation: Soothes skin discomfort, supports cellular turnover gently, and softens rough texture.
sensitivityNotes: Recognized by FDA as an OTC skin protectant; exceptionally gentle on irritated skin.
evidenceOrReference: FDA OTC Skin Protectant Monograph; CIR Final Report

plainLanguageExplanation: An oil-soluble acid that penetrates pores to loosen dead skin cells and clear trapped sebum.
sensitivityNotes: Can cause mild stinging, dryness, or peeling, especially when first introduced. Avoid if allergic to salicylates/aspirin.
evidenceOrReference: Journal of Clinical and Aesthetic Dermatology 2010; CIR Assessment

plainLanguageExplanation: A small-molecule alpha hydroxy acid that gently loosens surface dead skin cells to reveal smoother skin.
sensitivityNotes: Increases skin sensitivity to sunlight (requires daily sunscreen). May sting sensitive or damaged skin.
evidenceOrReference: CIR Safety Assessment 1998; FDA Guidance on AHAs

plainLanguageExplanation: Potent antioxidant that shields against environmental free radicals and helps fade dark spots.
sensitivityNotes: Requires an acidic pH (below 3.5) for stability in pure form, which can cause tingling or redness on sensitive skin.
evidenceOrReference: Dermatologic Surgery 2008; Journal of Investigative Dermatology

plainLanguageExplanation: Lipid-soluble antioxidant that protects product oils from oxidation and conditions the skin surface.
sensitivityNotes: Widely tolerated, though pure tocopheryl acetate can occasionally trigger allergic contact dermatitis in rare cases.
evidenceOrReference: CIR Safety Assessment 2018

plainLanguageExplanation: A lightweight, stable oil that mimics natural skin sebum to seal in moisture without a heavy feel.
sensitivityNotes: Very low comedogenicity and high skin compatibility across dry, combination, and oily skin.
evidenceOrReference: CIR Safety Assessment; International Journal of Cosmetic Science 2012

plainLanguageExplanation: A breathable silicone that gives products a silky slip and forms a protective moisture seal.
sensitivityNotes: Hypoallergenic and non-comedogenic in tested cosmetic concentrations.
evidenceOrReference: CIR Safety Assessment 2003; FDA Skin Protectant Monograph

plainLanguageExplanation: Helps dissolve active ingredients, adds slip to lotions, and draws moisture into the skin.
sensitivityNotes: One of the mildest glycols with a very low track record of contact allergy.
evidenceOrReference: CIR Safety Assessment 2018

plainLanguageExplanation: Prevents microbial growth, mold, and bacterial contamination, keeping the product safe to use over time.
sensitivityNotes: Safely regulated up to 1% in cosmetics. Sensitization is rare in the general adult population.
evidenceOrReference: Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety (SCCS) 2016; CIR Assessment

plainLanguageExplanation: Enhances the efficacy of preservatives while conditioning skin and softening the texture.
sensitivityNotes: Occasionally associated with rare contact allergic reactions; generally well tolerated.
evidenceOrReference: CIR Safety Assessment 2011

plainLanguageExplanation: A natural polysaccharide that thickens gels and emulsions, keeping ingredients uniformly mixed.
sensitivityNotes: Inert and non-sensitizing on human skin.
evidenceOrReference: CIR Safety Assessment 2016

plainLanguageExplanation: Reflects and scatters UVA and UVB rays, providing physical broad-spectrum sun protection.
sensitivityNotes: Ideal for sensitive, acne-prone, and rosacea-prone skin; also has gentle astringent properties.
evidenceOrReference: FDA Sunscreen Final Monograph; SCCS Opinion 2012

plainLanguageExplanation: Provides physical protection against UV radiation and provides whitening/opacity in formulations.
sensitivityNotes: Non-irritating for topical application on intact skin.
evidenceOrReference: FDA Sunscreen Monograph; SCCS 2014

plainLanguageExplanation: Added aromatic blend used to give the cosmetic formula a pleasant scent or mask base odors.
sensitivityNotes: One of the most frequent causes of cosmetic contact dermatitis. Those with reactive or allergy-prone skin may prefer fragrance-free options.
evidenceOrReference: American Academy of Dermatology (AAD); SCCS Opinion on Fragrance Allergens

plainLanguageExplanation: Prompts cell turnover and supports collagen synthesis to soften fine lines and smooth texture.
sensitivityNotes: Commonly causes peeling, dryness, and erythema during initial weeks of use ('retinization'). Requires sun protection.
evidenceOrReference: Clinical Interventions in Aging 2006; SCCS 2022

plainLanguageExplanation: Rich in polyphenol antioxidants (especially EGCG) that help protect skin from UV-induced oxidative stress.
sensitivityNotes: Very low irritation potential; frequently used in soothing and anti-pollution products.
evidenceOrReference: Oxidative Medicine and Cellular Longevity 2012; CIR 2019

plainLanguageExplanation: A liquid plant wax with a chemical profile similar to human sebum that softens and moisturizes skin.
sensitivityNotes: Non-greasy, gentle, and widely tolerated across varied skin types.
evidenceOrReference: CIR Safety Assessment 2008; Journal of Ethnopharmacology

plainLanguageExplanation: Binds to trace metal ions in water to prevent formula discoloration, rancidity, and breakdown.
sensitivityNotes: Used in very low percentages (<0.2%); low irritation potential in topical use.
evidenceOrReference: CIR Final Report on EDTA and its Salts
